2.content:
This Statement of Work covers Google Silicon COT Supply Chain Development, an implementation engagement to establish the data, process, and system foundations required for Google’s direct operating model with TSMC and OSAT partners across supplier visibility, ERP traceability, product test and quality, global trade compliance, and silicon supply planning. The engagement is intended to enable structured data exchange, lot-level traceability, and planning capabilities that treat yield and wafer-level constraints as core inputs, while scaling through a phased delivery model across E2Open, SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and the confirmed integration framework.

- Establish structured data flows and traceability across fabs, OSATs, and Google systems to support direct cost visibility and lot-level manufacturing control.
- Implement planning and execution capabilities that extend from finished-goods planning to wafer-level and yield-aware supply planning.
- Enable a phased foundation for quality, compliance, and operational adoption, including persona-driven change management and future analytical expansion.

Deferred scope decisions, assumptions, and open design points are identified in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
Google is establishing a Silicon COT supply chain capability that requires a clear baseline of current processes, systems, data, and organizational structures before finalizing the target design and implementation estimates. The current landscape spans SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and partner connectivity across foundry and OSAT operations, with key process areas including purchase order flow, subcontracting settlement, batch and lot traceability, full genealogy, master data, enterprise structure, and supply collaboration.

The engagement is driven by the need to address complexity in silicon planning and execution, including growth in data volume, scenario simulation, what-if planning, integration boundaries, and connectivity gaps between existing platforms and external partners. Google also needs to confirm whether the current Kinaxis environment has sufficient capacity and scalability to support silicon planning, or whether an alternative instance strategy is required based on performance, control, disruption tolerance, and cost.

This work is intended to define an executable To-Be blueprint for the Silicon BU, align process and data design to business requirements, and establish a scalable foundation for implementation across the confirmed in-scope geographies, legal entities, sites, and partner models.

3.2.content:
- Transition Google’s silicon supply chain from a black-box operating model to end-to-end manufacturing visibility, lot-level traceability, and structured auditability across wafer, die-bank, assembly, and finished-goods stages.
- Establish the Customer Owned Tooling (COT) operating model for the Silicon business, including direct collaboration with TSMC and identified OSAT partners.
- Define the future-state process and solution blueprint through AS-IS assessment, requirements gathering, and TO-BE finalization for Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and supporting partner-collaboration integrations.
- Configure Kinaxis as the primary planning layer to enable demand, supply, constraint, and scenario-based planning with yield- and capacity-aware decision support.
- Configure SAP S/4HANA PP/MM processes to support silicon manufacturing execution, material tracking, and supply-chain transactions aligned to the COT model.
- Enable integrated planning and partner collaboration through Kinaxis–SAP and E2Open-based data exchange for supplier commits, plan visibility, and execution alignment.
- Improve planning effectiveness through visibility to supplier commits versus plan, end-to-end WIP tracking, allocation and prioritization support, and reduced manual reconciliation.
- Deliver organizational change management, training, and end-user adoption tracking to support stakeholder readiness, user transition, and sustained process adoption across impacted functions.

3.3.content:
The target-state process flow supports Google’s transition to a direct COT model with SAP S/4HANA as the ERP and traceability backbone, E2Open as the external collaboration layer, and Kinaxis as the planning platform. Demand, forecast, commit, and purchase-order data flow between Google, TSMC, and OSAT partners through defined integrations, while SAP manages subcontracting, goods movements, batch/lot traceability, yield recording, supplier and organizational master data, and cost document capture.

At a high level, the process begins with demand and supply planning in Kinaxis, including yield-aware planning and die-bank visibility. Planning outputs, forecasts, and commit-related data are exchanged with external partners through E2Open, and procurement transactions are executed in SAP S/4HANA using inventory POs, schedule agreements, and subcontracting POs based on the approved partner model. Manufacturing execution progresses through wafer lot, probe, die bank, assembly, test, and finished goods stages with genealogy maintained at lot level in SAP. Cost, yield, and transactional data are captured through the process to support FICO integration, operational visibility, and downstream reporting and analytics.

The detailed target-state process flow, including any supporting diagram, will be finalized during the Explore phase after AS-IS validation and confirmation of the subcontractor/service-provider operating model. `<CONFIRM: include client-approved process-flow diagram if available>`

4.1.content:
- In scope geographies are Taiwan, Malaysia, and the United States, covering wafer manufacturing, OSAT processing, and downstream cross-border supply chain flows.
- Phase 1 includes Taiwan-based manufacturing and procurement activities, including TSMC, UMTC, and intra-Taiwan OSAT movements.
- Phase 2 expands scope to international execution and compliance flows, including Taiwan-to-United States export/import processes and Taiwan-to-Penang, Malaysia logistics flows.
- Additional countries, trade lanes, OSAT partner locations, and any WMS/TMS-enabled international logistics coverage are limited to those expressly confirmed during detailed design and approved through the change control process.

4.2.content:
Business processes in scope cover the Google Silicon Customer Owned Tooling (COT) supply chain across planning, manufacturing visibility, procurement, product test and quality, and related SAP-controlled inventory and lot traceability flows.

- End-to-end COT process visibility from wafer-out demand and supplier commits through wafer fabrication, probe, die bank, assembly, burn-in/unit test/SLT, QA/pack/ship, and rack/tray assembly and test.
- Production planning and materials management processes supporting wafer, raw material, substrate, HBM, die, lot, and finished-goods movements across TSMC, KYEC, SPIL, Google hub, and warehouse locations.
- Procurement processes for vendor master and scheduling agreement setup, wafer inventory purchase orders, substrate purchase orders, and OSAT subcontract purchase orders, including planned automation from Kinaxis where confirmed in design.
- Manufacturing operations processes including material master, bill of materials, subcontract PO structures, goods receipt flows, 4-step OSAT routing in SAP, lot genealogy, and WIP snapshots at defined handoff points.
- Product test and quality processes including wafer lot receipt, lot-level yield recording, in-process inspection at OSAT stages, test-data ingestion to the Silicon Data Hub, XY die-location fusion, and yield summary outputs to Kinaxis.
- Finance-adjacent operational processes required to support cost modeling, OSAT service-charge structures, actual costing against WIP events, yield-variance posting, and lot-level cost visibility in SAP; detailed FICO configuration remains Google-owned.
- Explore-phase process design activities to baseline current-state flows, define the target-state blueprint, confirm enterprise and partner organizational structures, and finalize process requirements for subcontracting, yield recording, traceability, transactional documents, and reporting.
- Constraint-based supply planning, inventory planning, analytics, and reporting processes supported through Kinaxis for the Silicon business unit.
- Excluded from this section unless later confirmed: processes outside the Silicon COT operating model and modules outside PP/MM-driven execution and the Google-owned controlling scope.

4.3.content:
- In scope are the technical design, configuration, and integration activities required to enable phased supply chain capabilities across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open Vendor Collaboration, Silicon Data Hub, BigQuery, SFTP-based data flows, and Amber Road for the agreed workstreams.
- SAP S/4HANA scope includes material master and bill of material support for wafer, raw materials, and substrate; TSMC inventory purchase order processing; OSAT subcontracting PO structures for SPIL and KYEC; full lot traceability from wafer through die, assembly, and finished goods; 4-step OSAT routing; actual costing runs; yield variance posting; scheduling agreement support for TSMC; UMTC substrate procurement; OSAT subcon POs; and SAP STO support for intra-Taiwan OSAT-to-OSAT movements.
- Kinaxis scope includes wafer demand signal integration to TSMC, planning BOM consumption from GPLM, basic wafer supply planning below SoC level via G-Plan, yield-adjusted netting, die bank buffering, OSAT capacity and constraint planning, automated demand signal and commit flows, full scenario simulation, multi-sourcing support, and COE governance support.
- E2Open scope includes TSMC structured commits, OSAT commit and recommit flows, OSAT WIP event visibility, ASN visibility, intra-Taiwan shipment visibility, Quanta ASN and proof-of-delivery visibility for the Taiwan-to-USA leg, and exception signal feedback to Kinaxis with automated management.
- Silicon Data Hub scope includes lot genealogy, wafer lot information capture at goods receipt, test data ingestion via SFTP, unit-level test data management, XY die location fusion, and in-process inspection data handling at OSAT stages.
- Analytics and reporting scope includes yield summaries to Kinaxis and finance analytics in BigQuery and the reporting layer.
- Trade compliance scope includes design and integration for Amber Road, with configuration of export and import documentation for Taiwan-to-USA flows in the applicable phases.
- Technical scope is phased: Phase 1 focuses on manufacturing visibility, Phase 2 on technical and business go-live plus hypercare, and Phase 3 on expanded scope including additional OSAT partner onboarding and international flow capabilities where confirmed.
- Google-owned and out-of-scope technical areas for Bristlecone include CO/FICO configuration and any material valuation, costing, yield accounting, TMS, EWM, and commercial invoice API work that is handled by Google internal teams or other designated parties.
- The detailed boundary for WMS/TMS and international flow enablement will be finalized as part of scope confirmation for Phase 3. <CONFIRM: whether WMS/TMS design and build are included or limited to logistics mapping/interface definition only>

4.4.content:
Bristlecone will provide program management and cross-functional solution delivery services for Google’s Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain implementation across Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open, using a phased Agile approach of Explore, Build, and Deploy.

Included services are:
- Project and program management, governance coordination, and phased release planning.
- Fit-gap analysis and to-be process design for end-to-end silicon planning and constrained supply planning.
- Functional and solution design covering Kinaxis Supply Planning, Constraint Planning, Inventory Planning, Analytics and Reporting, and related SAP S/4HANA PP/MM process integration.
- Configuration and build of the in-scope Kinaxis and SAP S/4HANA solution components.
- Integration analysis, design, and delivery for in-scope interfaces, including retention of Google’s existing integration framework where applicable and incremental delta interfaces identified during discovery.
- Functional specifications, data mapping support, and adaptation of existing data templates to support Silicon planning requirements.
- Test planning and execution support for unit testing, system integration testing, user acceptance testing, regression testing, and performance testing.
- Data migration and data load support for agreed in-scope objects and templates.
- Cutover planning, deployment support, and hypercare for phased go-lives.
- Organizational change management, training, knowledge transfer, and readiness support for business adoption.
- Collaboration with Google-assigned teams supporting adjacent areas, including controlling and other client-owned activities required for end-to-end execution.

Services will be delivered for the Silicon workstream across TSMC, KYEC, SPIL, Google Hub, and Warehouse locations, with a cross-functional delivery model spanning S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and integration resources. Any services not expressly listed in this Section 4.4 or expressly included elsewhere in this SOW are out of scope and subject to the Change Management Process in Section 17.

4.5.content:
The application scope covers Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open in support of Google’s Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain process.

- **Kinaxis**: Supply Planning, Constraint Planning, Inventory Planning, Analytics and Reporting, and Data Integration for wafer demand, yield-adjusted netting, die-bank planning, OSAT capacity visibility, demand and commit visibility, multi-sourcing, allocation, and scenario planning.
- **SAP S/4HANA**: Production Planning (PP) and Materials Management (MM) to support material master and bill of materials management, vendor and scheduling agreement setup, purchase order and goods receipt processing, subcon procurement structures, lot traceability, routing, inventory and goods movement transactions, and cost visibility across the Silicon supply chain.
- **E2Open**: Collaboration and integration support for inventory, purchase order, advance shipping, capacity, and contract manufacturer data exchanges across TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL.
- Application functionality in scope includes wafer-to-finished-goods traceability, lot and yield recording, constrained supply planning, inventory visibility, procurement signal enablement, and ERP-to-planning data synchronization across the in-scope application landscape.
- Finance, controlling, technical ABAP development, analytics, WMS/TMS, and trade-compliance application components are included only to the extent explicitly confirmed elsewhere in this SOW or approved during the Explore phase; Google’s internal team retains ownership of FICO configuration.
- Any additional application components, advanced analytics models, or future-route trade and logistics platforms not expressly listed above are outside scope unless added through the Change Management Process.

5.content:
The solution will use Kinaxis as the planning layer, SAP S/4HANA for execution and core supply chain transactions, and E2Open for supplier connectivity across the Silicon COT process. The architecture is designed to provide end-to-end visibility across TSMC and OSAT partners, align machine demand with silicon supply planning, and support yield-, capacity-, and inventory-aware decision making.

The deployment model will retain Google’s existing integration framework used for machine planning, with incremental delta interfaces added where required for Silicon planning. Existing data templates will be reused and updated to support Silicon planning needs. Kinaxis will be configured to consume additional inbound data from E2Open, including capacity information and CM data for TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. Delta integration using SAP BTP is in scope.

The initial deployment is scoped to Google Hub, Warehouse, and the Taiwan manufacturing network covering TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. Phased delivery will follow an Agile model across Explore, Build, and Deploy. Phase 1 and Phase 2 are based on Taiwan-only manufacturing flows, with broader geographic or process expansion addressed in later phases if approved.

Change governance will be managed through a cross-functional delivery structure spanning S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and integration workstreams. Architecture decisions that affect inventory ownership, procurement model, supplier onboarding sequence, or automated PO creation will be baselined during discovery and controlled through the formal change management process once approved. `<TECH TEAM: insert architecture diagram if available, showing Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, BTP, and external supplier interactions>`

6.1.content:
Bristlecone will deliver the engagement using a phased Agile methodology across S/4HANA and Kinaxis, with support for E2Open integrations as required. The delivery approach follows Explore, Build, and Deploy stages, with business process design completed before system configuration and with domain-led change management and role-based training embedded throughout execution.

The program will be executed as a wave-based rollout across three phases: Phase 1 and Phase 2 for MVP delivery, followed by Phase 3 for scaling. Delivery will align Google business and IT stakeholders with OSAT and foundry partners through regular weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, and quarterly governance reviews, with active tracking of milestones, risks, dependencies, and decisions.

Implementation activities will cover process design, application configuration, data integration, testing, deployment, and hypercare. The integration workstream will establish Kinaxis as the planning orchestration layer, maintain SAP as the execution backbone, enable supplier collaboration through E2Open, and support closed-loop planning through SAP ↔ Kinaxis integration, E2Open integration, GPlan/APIs, and the Silicon Data Hub.

Testing and release readiness will be managed through data-quality validation, System Integration Testing, User Acceptance Testing, and go-live readiness checks. Phase 3 will be delivered through a fixed-capacity rollout model, with the implementation team joining the current COE group to configure and deploy scaling scope, including `<CONFIRM: final Phase 3 E2Open rollout details if applicable>`.

7.1.content:
Project governance will operate at three levels: workstream delivery reviews, program-level decision reviews, and executive escalation for scope, timeline, or commercial matters requiring cross-functional resolution. Governance will align to the phased implementation plan for Manufacturing Visibility, Business Go-Live, and Expanded Scope, with decisions tracked against phase readiness and dependency closure.

- Workstream leads from Google and Bristlecone will review scope progress, open decisions, dependencies, and blockers for each in-scope workstream.
- Program governance will consolidate cross-workstream status, phase readiness, key risks, and decisions affecting SAP, Kinaxis, E2Open, Silicon Data Hub, and related integration dependencies.
- Executive governance will address unresolved escalations, milestone risks, scope changes, and business decisions that affect committed timelines, including the Dec 4 TSMC PO readiness requirement.
- Issues will be escalated first within the relevant workstream, then to the program leadership team, and then to executive sponsors if resolution affects phase scope, delivery dates, commercials, or client obligations.
- Deferred decisions, including Google confirmation points that affect inventory ownership, logistics design, or phase boundaries, must be resolved before the impacted design or build activities proceed.
- Phase 3 scope expansion, including additional OSAT partner onboarding and any confirmed international flow components, will be governed through formal scope review and change control before execution.

Governance cadence, named forums, and approvers will be confirmed during project mobilization and documented in the project plan: `<CONFIRM: governance cadence and named client/Bristlecone escalation roles>`.

7.3.content:
- Work will be performed in a phased Agile model across Explore, Build, Deploy, Hypercare, and handover to the current COE group.
- Phase 3 is planned from April 2027 through December 2027 and covers HFC-related work, future procurement cycles, and onboarding of new OSATs.
- The implementation schedule includes data load, configuration, testing, deployment, and hypercare activities aligned to the agreed phase plan.
- OCM activities will run in parallel with delivery and include awareness and assessment, communications, training, readiness checks, and hypercare support.
- Bristlecone will manage the project timeline, monitor execution and blockers, lead defect triage and issue escalation, and support cutover, go-live, hypercare, and handover activities in accordance with the agreed RACI.
- Google will provide timely decisions, updated product flows, data inputs, environment readiness, and business participation required to maintain the planned schedule.
- The implementation team will join the existing COE organization with fixed capacity to configure and roll out the Phase 3 scope.
- Detailed working hours, holiday calendar alignment, and any required overlap across delivery locations will be confirmed during project initiation.

8.content:
- Project personnel shall be proficient in English and able to conduct design workshops, playback sessions, training, and governance discussions with Google business and IT stakeholders.

- Team members shall have demonstrated experience in semiconductor supply chain and adjacent manufacturing/distribution operations, including planning, logistics, trade compliance, and plant localization requirements.

- Functional and technical resources shall be familiar with global-template design, fit-to-standard workshops, baseline configuration, localization capture, gap analysis, and solution sign-off processes for large transformation programs.

- Assigned personnel shall have working knowledge of SAP S/4HANA delivery practices, Kinaxis planning processes and data flows, integration design, security role analysis, data migration, testing, and cutover/hypercare support.

- Resources supporting design and documentation shall be able to prepare and maintain business process designs, key design decisions, configuration documents, training materials, test artifacts, knowledge-transfer materials, and SOPs in the project-approved formats and standards.

- Project team members shall be experienced in structured delivery methodologies, including fit-to-standard workshop execution, phased implementation planning, stakeholder enablement, and formal design/readout sign-off.

- Change management and training resources shall be experienced in stakeholder mapping, readiness assessment, communications planning, train-the-trainer execution, and adoption support across business functions.

- Personnel qualifications and certifications shall be as described in Appendix B, including any project-required product, methodology, or domain certifications `<CONFIRM: required certifications, if any>`.

- Freeze all deferred scope decisions, including integration design, data-load approach, and localization requirements, before build sprints start; route any later change through Section 17.

16.1 Milestone Deliverables Matrix 
A milestone deliverables matrix shall be maintained from project mobilization through hypercare and updated at each phase gate. The matrix shall identify each committed deliverable, planned due date, responsible owner, dependency, acceptance criterion, and sign-off authority, and shall align to the project plan, deliverables list, and invoicing milestones.

16.2 Deferred Scope Decisions 
- Any open design or scope decision shall be logged before execution of the affected work begins. 
- Deferred decisions with timeline, effort, or commercial impact shall be reviewed through the governance structure and resolved by the agreed decision owners. 
- Work dependent on unresolved decisions shall not proceed beyond approved assumptions without written approval through the change control process. 
- Current decision items include clarification of the SAP to E2Open invoice receipt and 3-way match scope, payment processing responsibilities for subcontractor/vendor settlement, and any remaining localization requirements. 

16.3 Integration & Custom Code Safeguards 
- Integration scope shall be baselined and tracked by interface, including SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, SAP MM, SAP CO, and Big Query touchpoints in scope. 
- Custom development shall be governed through a finalized RICEFW list, approved functional and technical specifications, and traceability to business requirements. 
- Any increase in interface count, custom object volume, or localization-driven build effort beyond the approved baseline shall be assessed for schedule and commercial impact and processed through change control before execution. 
- Mock data loads, unit testing, SIT, UAT, cutover readiness, and production support readiness shall be used as control points before release progression. 

16.4 Change Control 
All scope, timeline, resource, and commercial changes shall follow the Change Management Process in Section 17. Governance forums shall review open risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, and change requests on a regular cadence, with escalation to the project steering structure for items requiring client decisions or approval.

- Acceptance criteria for each phase and deliverable will be defined in measurable terms before execution, including completion evidence, entry and exit criteria, and named reviewer ownership.
- Test planning will cover test plan and test case creation, test execution, defect resolution, retest, test closure, and Go/No-Go decisions against agreed exit criteria.
- Quality validation will include Unit Test, System Integration Test, and User Acceptance Test aligned to the phased delivery approach.
- Unit Test will validate configuration and development at the functionality level in the development environment, with results documented and peer reviewed.
- System Integration Test will validate end-to-end process performance across integrated systems in the test/quality environment using representative data volumes and core team participation.
- User Acceptance Test will validate that the solution meets business requirements using business-scenario-based test scripts prepared by Bristlecone and executed by Google end users in the test/quality environment.
- Defects identified during testing will be logged, assigned, corrected or stabilized through approved workarounds, and returned for retest before closure.
- Progression between test cycles and release phases will be subject to Go/No-Go review against agreed exit criteria; items that do not meet acceptance criteria will be remediated through the project plan or formal change control, as applicable.
- Bristlecone recommends that acceptance criteria in Sections 9 and 11 be finalized at deliverable level, not only at phase level, and tied to sign-off owners and due dates before build start.

- Bristlecone resources assigned to this engagement shall have demonstrated experience in Kinaxis supply planning, SAP S/4HANA planning and master-data processes, integration coordination, and organizational change management relevant to a silicon supply chain implementation.

- Core delivery capabilities shall include planning business rules and functionality design for demand, supply, inventory, and constraint-aware planning; validation of data requirements for BOM, yield, capacity, sourcing, part, site, WIP, inventory, and supplier-commit inputs; and cross-functional coordination across Kinaxis, S/4HANA, E2Open, PLM, and reporting stakeholders.

- The delivery team is expected to include program leadership, solution architecture, process consulting, Kinaxis consulting, integration architecture and consulting, SAP PP/MM functional support, and OCM leadership and consulting, with a blended onsite and offshore model aligned to the approved staffing plan.

- Personnel supporting implementation shall be proficient in collaborative delivery methods, requirements validation, test support, defect triage, cutover readiness, and business-user enablement.

- OCM resources shall be capable of persona-based adoption planning, targeted communications, role-based training, stakeholder engagement, and super-user/change-ambassador enablement for planner and sourcing user groups impacted by the future-state process.

- Technical and functional resources shall be familiar with planning data structures and process dependencies including multi-level BOMs, yield parameters by manufacturing stage, sourcing and network rules, resource-capacity constraints, demand transfers, safety-stock logic, on-hand inventory, WIP, open POs, supplier commits, and constrained versus unconstrained planning outputs.
